text: Thank you for that initial detail, and I have noted your Audiogram results. speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The duration of three minutes, lack of persistent hearing loss, and the sudden onset strongly suggest BPPV rather than Meniere's or a central stroke. To confirm this, I need you to perform the Dix-Hallpike maneuver; please stand up and lean back suddenly with your head turned 45 degrees to the right. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain (to rule out central causes if you have any other neurological deficits).
